text:
jess_support: Escalating — customer hit go module errors after upgrading to our Go SDK v2 tag. They say builds break on CI, and local 'go get' fails. Pasting their minimal repro and logs below. @carl_engineer can you take a look?

jess_support: Customer repo snippet:```
module github.com/customer/app

require (
  github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
)
```

jess_support: Error they see:```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: parsing go.mod: unexpected module path "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2"

# or sometimes:
# go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: module declares its path: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2
```

dana_customer: FWIW we also had a local replace in go.mod to test a fork:```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../go-sdk-local
```

dana_customer: CI fails because our CI doesn't have that local path, so dependency resolution just errors out.

carl_engineer: This is the classic v2+ module path mismatch. When a module's go.mod declares module "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2" the consumers must require/import the /v2 path. They probably published v2 tag but updated module path, or vice versa.

carl_engineer: Quick checks to run (steps to reproduce):
1) clone their repo
2) ensure GOPROXY is default
3) run `go mod tidy` or `go get ./...` -> you should see the parsing error above

mike_gomod: Output we saw in a local repro:```
$ go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0
go: finding module for package github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk
go: downloading github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
go: found github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk in github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: parsing go.mod: unexpected module path "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2"
```

carl_engineer: Root cause possibilities: either the published tag v2.0.0's archive contains a go.mod with module path ending in /v2 (recommended for semver v2), but the consumer required the non-/v2 path (github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0). Or the repo module path doesn't include /v2 but tags were created as v2.x causing confusion.

dana_customer: We never changed our import lines (we import github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk). We assumed the tag bump would keep compatibility.

carl_engineer: Fixes / workarounds for customers: short term: change require to the major path:```
require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0
```
and update imports to:```
import "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2"
```
Then `go mod tidy` should succeed.

carl_engineer: If you cannot change imports immediately (large codebase), as a temporary workaround you can use a replace to point the old import path to the new module path in your go.mod, e.g.:```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0
```
But that is ugly and we should not recommend long-term.

mike_gomod: On the publishing side (internal): ensure the module's go.mod declares the correct module path for v2+: `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and that release tags are created as `v2.0.1` etc. If you published v2 tag but left the module path without /v2 then consumers will see other errors.

carl_engineer: Action items: 1) @mike_gomod can you verify the tag v2.0.0 contents on the repo (go.mod module line + tree layout)? 2) @infra-bot can we check the release artifacts and CI publishing step for the go-sdk to confirm the archive on GitHub has the correct go.mod? 3) @dana_customer try the require/import change above and report back.

infra-bot: Scheduled job queued: artifact-inspector for repo github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk tag v2.0.0 (job id 9853). Will post results here. :robot_face: 

mike_gomod: I pulled the v2.0.0 tag locally — its go.mod has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`. The tag exists and the archive on GitHub includes that go.mod. Looks correct for v2 semantics.

mike_gomod: Most likely the customer's project still references the old import path. We should update docs & release notes to call out the migration (import path must include /v2). I'll open a tiny patch to the README.

dana_customer: Confirmed — switching to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` in our go.mod and imports fixed local `go mod tidy`. CI still needs the replace removed and clean tags; we'll re-run.

jess_support: Great — please follow up if CI still fails after cleans. Recording this for knowledge base: publish note about Go module major-version import path requirement and a recommended migration snippet.

carl_engineer: One more gotcha to document: tagged releases uploaded via some release tooling sometimes rewrite go.mod or strip /v2 in the archive root; verify release zip content. Also mention consumers who vendor deps may need to refresh vendor/ or run `go mod vendor`.

jess_support: Closing the loop — if CI passes for customer, we'll mark resolved and add KB entry. Thanks everyone. :tada:
